title: Competitor telemetry synthesis and inference readiness audit
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: synthesize publicly observable and partner-sourced telemetry about competitor model endpoints (latency distributions, throttling/failover patterns, regional availability, quantization/compatibility variants) and produce a prioritized inference-readiness audit that maps where Redwood must harden fallbacks, routing, or quantization guidance.

Scope:
- Public telemetry scraping of provider status pages, API error rate trends, and release notes (last 6 months)
- Partner / customer-reported incidents and availability signatures (sanitized)
- Synthetic probes targeting typical Redwood usage profiles: short-chat (<=128 tokens), long-generation (>=1024 tokens), embeddings, and streaming sessions
- Evaluation of compatibility signals: API contract deviations, structured output differences, function-calling stability, and quantization artifacts that affect model substitutability
- Output: an audit doc with prioritized risk buckets and tactical mitigations (routing, canary variants, pre-warmed capacity recommendations) and a short ops playbook for 3 highest-risk markets/regions.
acceptance_criteria: Collected telemetry cover at least 5 public providers and 2 partner reports for each region (NA/EU/APAC)
Synthetic probe dataset executed for 4 workload archetypes and results ingested into a canonical dashboard (latency percentiles, error codes, throughput)
Audit ranks top 8 risk scenarios with clear mitigation owners (PM/Eng/SE) and estimated effort
Patchable mitigations (routing fallback rules, pre-warm recipes, quantization guidance) documented and linked to follow-up tickets
Presentation delivered to PM-Infra + Solutions on the cycle demo and feedback captured
